title: Three Years of r/ChatGPT: Societal Impact Evaluations from Social Media Data
one_liner: Treat a large user forum as a stream of behavior reports, classify the kinds of use people discuss over time, and detect when sensitive uses start rising before formal institutions react.
lead: Widely used consumer AI systems change daily life before formal surveys, policy studies, or product disclosures can catch up. This paper uses r/ChatGPT as a real-time measurement channel for those changes. The key move is not merely scraping posts. It builds a framework for identifying categories of social impact, tracking how often they appear over time, and distinguishing long-run normalization from sudden shifts after specific product events. The paper's concrete finding is that discussion of everyday routine use grows steadily, while posts about mental health support and emotional attachment rise after GPT-4o launched in May 2024 and become detectable months before public acknowledgment.

problem.h2: Why product impact moves faster than standard evaluation
paras: A consumer AI product can change habits, relationships, and support-seeking behavior long before a formal study is designed and run. Surveys take time to field. Interviews are expensive. Product teams may not disclose internal usage patterns quickly. That leaves a gap between real adoption and public understanding.

Social media partly fills that gap because users voluntarily describe what they are doing, what feels new, and what worries them. But raw post counts are noisy. A larger subreddit does not automatically mean larger impact, and one viral topic can distort perception. The paper therefore asks for a principled measurement pipeline: define impact categories, classify posts into those categories, model their frequency over time, and check whether emerging patterns appear early enough to matter for monitoring.

callout.html: The useful signal is not that people talk about ChatGPT a lot. It is that the mix of topics changes in measurable ways that reveal new forms of dependence, normalization, or risk.

steps.text: Gather posts from the subreddit across multiple years. This matters because one short window cannot distinguish early-curiosity spikes from lasting adoption.
Specify what kinds of use or concern the study is trying to measure. This matters because otherwise the analysis collapses very different behaviors into one noisy trend.

steps.b: 3. Classify posts by category over time
steps.text: Assign posts to categories such as everyday use, mental health support, or emotional attachment. This matters because the signal lies in category frequency, not in raw post volume alone.
Check both full-history patterns and what a live monitor would have seen at each point in time. This matters because a good explanation of the past may still fail as an early-warning system.
Look for topic changes around major launches such as GPT-4o in May 2024. This matters because timing helps separate product-driven shifts from background forum drift.

paras: The paper changes the data source for societal impact evaluation from periodic studies to an always-on public discussion stream. That does not replace formal evaluation, but it creates a monitoring object that can move at the speed of product adoption.
object.object: a real-time social-impact monitoring signal built from forum discussion

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: topic prevalence conditional on adoption
hidden.name: how the composition of discussion changes after adoption becomes routine
paras: A growing forum can hide two opposite stories. It can mean more people are doing ordinary productive tasks, or it can mean a smaller but important category of sensitive uses is growing inside a much larger stream. The hidden quantity is not total discussion volume. It is the prevalence of each impact category relative to the changing baseline of adoption and discussion volume.

That is why the paper emphasizes normalization and trend detection. Once early-curiosity posting fades, a rise in emotional attachment posts is more informative than raw posting volume because it says a different social use is taking a larger share of the discussion, not just that more people are talking overall.

heat.caption: Highlighted cells mark category shifts that remain visible even after accounting for the forum's overall growth and normalization.

reads.html: The important change is which uses take up more of the conversation once the product is already normal, not only how many total posts exist.
Longitudinal category prevalence provides a finer social-impact signal than total volume because it isolates shifts in use patterns from generic growth in product awareness.

mechanism.h2: Why it works: repeated public self-reports expose behavior change
paras: Users describe their own practices in public forums because they want advice, validation, or community discussion. Those posts are noisy at the individual level, but they become informative in aggregate when grouped by impact category and tracked over long periods. The mechanism is therefore repeated weak measurement: each post is a partial observation, and the time series of many posts reveals durable changes in how the product is used.

The real-time monitor works because harmful or sensitive uses often emerge as a gradual share increase before institutions respond. A sudden rise in posts about emotional dependence does not need every post to be perfectly labeled. It only needs enough signal for the category's prevalence to move persistently above baseline. Anchoring those shifts to product events matters because feature changes alter what users can do and how they relate to the system. The paper's detection result is therefore not just correlation with news cycles. It is a test of whether the live monitoring pipeline would have surfaced the shift months earlier.

stages.s: Three years of subreddit posts and timestamps
Compare trajectories before and after product events
Run a real-time detector for sustained unusual growth
An early signal of changing societal impact patterns

math.h2: The key signal is category share over time
math.words: For each time period, count how many posts fall into a category and divide by the total number of posts in that period. Trend detection then asks whether that share rises persistently after a product event or beyond baseline noise.
symbols: number of posts assigned to one impact category in time period t
all observed posts in the same time period
share of discussion devoted to that category at time t

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose October has 1,000 posts and 40 of them are about emotional attachment. The prevalence is 40 divided by 1,000, which is 4 percent.
Suppose November has 1,500 posts and 90 of them are about emotional attachment. The prevalence is 90 divided by 1,500, which is 6 percent.
Raw counts went up by 50 posts, but the share also rose from 4 percent to 6 percent.
That second fact is the informative one because it shows the topic is taking a larger fraction of discussion rather than merely appearing more often because the subreddit got bigger.

math.note: A prevalence trend is more informative than a raw count trend when the total forum size is changing quickly.

items.b: Forum users are not the whole user base.
items.html: Reddit posters are a selected population with their own age, language, and participation biases. A trend on the forum may miss important impacts in populations that do not post there because the measurement channel is partial.

items.b: Category labels can blur intent and experience.
items.html: A post about mental health could be a joke, a critique, or a genuine support-seeking report. Misclassification noise matters because the detector only sees category assignments, not direct ground truth about the user's life.

items.b: Product events are not the only moving cause.
items.html: Media coverage, school calendars, labor market shocks, or moderation changes can also shift what people post. Linking a rise to one model launch requires caution because multiple outside changes can happen near the same time.
Treat forum monitoring as an early signal generator, then pair it with surveys, interviews, or platform-side evidence when a category begins rising enough to suggest a real social change.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a timeline view over a labeled subset of forum posts. Let the user select categories such as everyday use, mental health support, and emotional attachment, then show both raw counts and prevalence by month. Mark a product event such as the May 2024 GPT-4o launch and simulate a real-time detector that only sees data up to each month. The demo should show that a rising category share becomes visible before a human reading the full history retrospectively would naturally treat it as an established trend.
demo.closing: A successful demo shows that social-impact monitoring can produce an actionable warning window instead of only a retrospective narrative.
